newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo building death toll reaches 63.
newsitem.headline: Cairo building death toll reaches 63.

text.p: Rescue workers have retrieved 63 bodies from the apartment block which collapsed in the Cairo suburb of Heliopolis on Sunday, army officers said on Saturday.
"We don't think there are any left now, more or less," added an army brigadier organising clearance of the rubble.

Bulldozers and other heavy equipment have moved most of the debris from the collapsed part of the 11-storey building and cranes will move in soon to demolish a section at the back which remains standing and which is confirmed clear of bodies.

The workers have left one section of the debris because it contains radioactive material from a radiology centre which was in the building, the brigadier said. "We want to make sure it's removed safely," he added.
The most widely accepted theory is that the building collapsed because workers cut away some of the pillars during modifications to the offices of a banking organisation.
The government, reacting to public outrage, has toughened the penalties for breaking building regulations.
